L100: # UMass Global Application Process: Step-by-Step Guide
L101: 
L102: By:
L103: 
L104: UMass Global
L105: 
L106: Published: March 9th, 2026
L107: 
L108: 【52†Image: student doing online school work. 】
L109: 
L110: Deciding to earn your degree at University of Massachusetts Global is an exciting and a significant first step in your journey! UMass Global fosters a culture of support that helps students achieve their educational goals.
L111: ## UMass Global Application Process: How To Apply and Start Classes
L112: 
L113: Now what does the full process from inquiry to the start of classes look like for a prospective student? Let’s dive into each of the steps you will need to take to start classes.
L114: ### Step 1: Connect with Your Enrollment Coach
L115: 
L116: Your journey at UMass Global begins with a call with our Enrollment Coaching Center, where you will be assigned a dedicated enrollment coach. Think of them as your personal guide through the admissions process. During that first conversation, your coach will answer initial questions, explain what to expect, and help you explore programs that match your interests and goals, and walk you through our transfer policy and the rest of the admissions process.
L117: From that first call to admission, your coach is there to make sure your path to enrollment is clear, supported, and tailored to your needs.
L118: 
L119: Who to contact? Speak with an enrollment coach at (800) 746-0082 or email enroll@umassglobal.edu.
L120: ### Step 2: Submit Your Application and Required Documents
L121: 
L122: Once you’re confirmed UMass Global is a good fit, it’s time to apply! The application is simple, free, and available to complete online. After you submit it, you’ll get an email with a link to your personal Application Dashboard — a one-stop hub for tracking your progress. There, you’ll find a checklist of required documents, deadlines, and next steps to keep you on track.
L123: Application deadlines are two weeks prior to the start of the program. So, be sure to give yourself ample time to request transcripts, discuss your academic plan with your coach, and explore financial options. You can view current deadlines and start dates here: 【29†Apply Now | UMass Global】.
L124: We want your application process to be as seamless as possible, so we’ve designed these steps to help you along the way. Because the process may look a little different depending on your program or level, we’ll walk you through what to expect in the following sections.
L125: 
L126: Who to contact? Call (800) 746-0082 or email apply@umassglobal.edu.
L127: #### Undergraduate Applicants
L128: 
L129: Undergraduate students who are applying for an associate or bachelor’s degree.
L130: 
L131: Undergraduate Admission Requirements
L132: 
L133: To begin your educational journey at UMass Global, you first must be admitted as an undergraduate (associate and bachelor’s degree candidates). For admission, you’ll need to meet the following requirements:
L134: 
L135: You’ll need to have completed high school or have an equivalent level of education. To verify that, we accept any of these documents:
L136:   * A high school diploma or transcript
L137:   * A General Education Development (GED) certificate
L138:   * A state-authorized high school equivalency certificate or diploma
L139:   * A state-recognized home study certificate or transcript
L140:   * Documentation from an approved foreign evaluation service certifying international coursework equivalent to a U.S. high school diploma
L141: 
L142: In addition to the above, there may be additional specific requirements for the program you want to enroll in.
L143:   * Undergrads without 12 transferable college credits, equaling a combined GPA of 2.0 or higher, will start their UMass Global journey in LBSU 100 Student Success Strategies during the first session.
L144: This course is designed to set you up for success from day one, giving you practical tools for college-level work — like stronger study skills, helpful test-taking approaches, better time management, and stress-reduction techniques — so you can feel more confident and stay on track as you move through your program.
L145:   * If past academic performance doesn’t reflect your current ability, UMass Global’s Academic Fresh Start program can help you begin with a clean slate.
L146: To confirm any additional admission needs, check the academic catalog and talk with your assigned enrollment coach to ensure you meet all undergraduate requirements for your specific program.
L147: 
L148: How to Submit Your Undergraduate Application
L149: 
L150: To apply for an undergraduate program, please submit:
L151:   * Your online application, including a list of every college/university/career institution/military institution/etc. where you earned academic credit.
L152:   * Official transcripts from all prior institutions.
L153:   * TIP: Upload your unofficial transcripts to your application for expedited admission.
L154:   * Official transcripts will be required by the end of your first session.
L155:   * UMass Global will attempt to order official transcripts from all institutions listed on your application. However, some institutions do not allow 3rd party ordering, so check your email for confirmation.
L156: Please note: Missing transcripts will delay the application process, so be sure all institutions are included. Electronic transcripts should be sent directly from the issuing school to the UMass Global Admissions Office at admtranscripts@umassglobal.edu.
L157: 
L158: For paper transcripts, all documents must arrive at the Admissions Office in a sealed envelope from the institution of record. Mail all transcripts to:
L159: University of Massachusetts Global
L160: ATTN: Office of Admission
L161: 65 Enterprise, Suite 150
L162: Aliso Viejo, CA 92656
L163: 
L164: To walk you through it, we’ve created this helpful 【53†undergrad admissions video†share.synthesia.io】 you can use as a guide. For additional questions, reach out to your enrollment coach for support.

L172: Who to contact? Call (800) 746-0082 or email apply@umassglobal.edu.
L173: #### Graduate Applicants
L174: 
L175: Graduate students who are applying for a master’s or doctoral degree.
L176: 
L177: Graduate Admission Requirements
L178: 
L179: There are three ways to qualify for graduate admission:
L180: 
L181: 1. By minimum grade point average
L182: 
L183:   * Applicants must have a minimum GPA of 2.75 in their most recently completed degree. (Note: Some graduate programs require a minimum GPA of 3.0. Please refer to the university catalog for specific program requirements.)
L184: 
L185: 2. By prior graduate degree
L186:   * You hold a completed master’s degree (or higher) from an accredited institution.
L187: 
L188: 3. By submitting a portfolio
L189: 
L190:   * Submit a portfolio showing readiness for grad school, including: writing samples, resume, awards, letters of recommendation, and an explanation of why you’re a strong candidate. If your portfolio is approved, you may be invited to interview. The final admission decision rests with the Graduate Admissions Committee.
L191: 
L192: UMass Global does not require GRE scores for admission.
L193: How to Submit Your Graduate Application + Required Documents
L194: 
L195: To apply for any graduate program (degree, certificate, or credential), please submit:
L196:   * Your online application, stating where you earned your highest degree (bachelor's, master's, or doctoral).
L197:   * Official transcripts from the accredited institution where you earned your highest degree.
L198:     * TIP: Upload your unofficial transcript to your application for expedited admission.
L199:     * Official transcripts will be required by the end of your first session.
L200:   * Additional transcripts or documents may be requested for specific programs.
L201:   * Any extra materials required by your chosen program.
L202: Electronic transcripts should be sent directly from the issuing school to the UMass Global Admissions Office at admtranscripts@umassglobal.edu.
L203: 
L204: For paper transcripts, all documents must arrive at the Admissions Office in a sealed envelope from the institution of record. Mail all transcripts to:
L205: 
L206: University of Massachusetts Global
L207: ATTN: Office of Admission
L208: 65 Enterprise, Suite 150
L209: Aliso Viejo, CA 92656
L210: Our 【55†graduate admissions video†share.synthesia.io】 can help walk you through this process. For additional questions, reach out to your enrollment coach for support.

L218: Who to contact? Call (800) 746-0082 or email apply@umassglobal.edu.
L219: #### International Applicants
L220: 
L221: To apply, international students will need to complete the following three steps:
L222: 
L223: Step 1: Complete Transcript Evaluation
L224: 
L225: You will need to attain a course-by-course transcript evaluation from 【57†International Education Research Foundation†ierf.org】 (IREF), 【58†World Education Services†wes.org】, or other 【59†National Association of Credential Evaluation Services†naces.org】 (NACES) accredited member institution.
L226: These evaluations must be dated within one year and must include:
L227: 
L228:   * A course-by-course report.
L229:   * A copy of the official academic transcripts used by the evaluation agency.
L230: 
L231: Step 2: Upload Your Documents
L232: 
L233: As an international student, you must submit all required documents directly through the online application portal.
L234: 
L235: Step 3: Submit Your Online Application:
L236: 
L237: Lastly, you will need to complete and submit your application for review.
L238: 
L239: Who to contact? Call (800) 746-0082 or email apply@umassglobal.edu.
L240: #### Returning Student Applicants
L241: 
L242: Returning students will fall into two buckets; less than 2 years leave, and more than 2 years leave.
L243: 
L244: Students returning after less than two years are still considered active. In this case, your first step is to schedule an appointment with an academic advisor to review your most recent educational plan and create an updated return plan. After that, you’ll connect with a one-stop specialist to discuss payment options and finalize your re-enrollment.
L245: Who to contact? Call (800) 746-0082 or email acadadvisorol@umassglobal.edu.
L246: Students returning after more than two years are considered inactive and will need to restart the admissions process. The first step is to contact the Enrollment Coaching Center to begin reapplying. Previously submitted transcripts remain on file in your student records and do not need to be resubmitted. However, if you’ve completed any new coursework since leaving UMass Global, you’ll need to provide official transcripts from those institutions.
L247: Who to contact? Call (800) 746-0082 or email enroll@umassglobal.edu.
L248: ### Step 3: Processing, Acceptance, and Next Steps
L249: 
L250: Students can track their admission status through the application portal. If admitted, you will be notified of your acceptance by email from the Office of Admission and by phone from your enrollment coach. After you submit all required application documents, your admission review typically takes about 3–10 business days, depending on your academic level and program.
L251: Please note: admitted doesn’t mean committed — you still have time to ask questions, explore financial options, and confirm you are ready to move forward before signing your final financial agreement.
L252: Once admitted, your enrollment coach will set up a new student appointment for you with an academic advisor. You will then receive a Calendly appointment link that contains the agreed upon date and time, the academic advisor’s name, and the Zoom room link to the advisor’s meeting room. This is where you will officially be introduced to your academic advisor, who will remain with you through your degree program.
L253: If you lose contact information, you can always find the name of your advisor on your student Degreeworks page. Your advisor will show you how to access this page during your appointment and will share a link to it in a follow-up email as well.
L254: Your academic advisor will then help you create a personalized education plan tailored to your goals, schedule, and selected program. Our advisors will also guide you through:
L255:   * Selecting courses that align with your interests and fulfill degree requirements.
L256:   * Staying on track to graduate by mapping out each term and checking in to help you adjust your plan as needed.
L257:   * Ensure your program remains flexible and manageable by helping you decide course loads and formats that fit your work, family, and life commitments.
L258: 
L259: From admission to graduation, your advisor remains a consistent source of support and guidance.
L260: ### Step 4: Financial Planning
L261: 
L262: After you have been admitted, submit the 【25†UMass Global Scholarship Verification Form】 to see if you may be eligible for a UMass Global scholarship.
L263: 
L264: During your initial new student appointment, your advisor will work with you to set up a meeting with a one-stop specialist who will help you build a plan for financing your education.
L265: 
L266: One-stop specialists will help you explore ways to pay for school and guide you through your selected plan, which may include:
L267:   * Identifying required documents for your specific financial plan.
L268:   * Providing financial guidance and literacy.
L269:   * Explaining how specific benefits work including military or partnership benefits.
L270:   * Guidance through scholarships, tuition and fees, textbook ordering, financial aid, and the FAFSA process.
L271:   * Assistance with registering for classes.
L272: One-stop works with active duty, VA students, and VA vocational rehab students, as well as partner students, state vocational rehab students, and cash paying students. After your one-stop appointment, expect a follow-up email that includes a summary of your financial funding choices, any steps you need to complete, and helpful university resources and tools.
L273: 
L274: While each student has a dedicated advisor, you can call into the one-stop department and speak with any specialist for assistance.
L275: Processing Financial Aid
L276: 
L277:   * After you meet with one-stop, you will submit your financial aid application to the Financial Aid Office.
L278:   * The Financial Aid Office will review the application and process your award accordingly.
L279:   * You will then receive an award letter via your student email detailing the financial aid awarded to you.
L280:   * You must sign the award and send it back to the Financial Aid Office signaling acceptance.
L281: ### Step 5: Preparing for Your First Class
L282: 
L283: To prepare for classes, you should complete the online New Student Orientation (in Brightspace), review your course schedule thoroughly, and connect with student support services to make sure you’re ready for your first day. New students are given access to Brightspace about 3 days after being admitted. Once enrolled, you will have access to your courses in Brightspace at 5:00 p.m. PDT on the Friday before the class begins (classes always start on a Monday).
L284: UMass Global’s additional support services include:
L285: 
L286:   * 【60†Accessible Education Services】
L287:   * 【61†AI Career Services Hub】
L288:   * 【62†Library†umassglobal.libguides.com】
L289:   * 【33†Military Support】
L290:   * 【63†Tutoring and Academic Support†umassglobal.libguides.com】
L291: 
L292: Many degree programs begin six times per year, so you can start whenever you’re ready!
L293: 
L294: Who to contact? Direct any questions you have to your assigned Academic Advisor.
L295: ## Have Other Questions or Need Additional Support? We’re Here to Help
L296: 
L297: Starting your journey at UMass Global is an exciting decision, and we’re committed to supporting you every step of the way. If you have any questions about the admissions process, programs, or next steps, reach out to an enrollment coach at (800) 746-0082. Our team is ready to help you find the answers you need and make your path to enrollment as smooth as possible.
L298: Wanting more information on the admission's process timeline? Explore our 【64†admissions roadmap】.

L119: #### [Button: Who can assist me with the application process? ]
L120: 
L121: Your enrollment coach is your main point of contact for your application status, requirements, and next steps. They can answer most general questions about programs, deadlines, and what to submit, and will help you stay on track as you move toward enrollment.​
L122: 
L123: If you have not yet been contacted by an enrollment coach, you can call (800) 746-0082 or email enroll@umassglobal.edu to be connected with someone who can support you.
L124: #### [Button: How can I check on my admissions status? ]
L125: 
L126: Follow these steps to view your status and any remaining items:
L127:   1. After you submit your application, look for an email from UMass Global with a link to your Application Dashboard.​
L128:   2. Go to the online application page and 【53†Sign In†apply.umassglobal.edu】.​
L129:   3. Log in using the same email and password you used when you first completed your application.​
L130:   4. Once you are on the Application Dashboard, you can:
L131:      * View your current admission status.
L132:      * See any outstanding documents or program requirements needed to complete your application.
L133: #### [Button: When will I find out if I’m admitted, and how will I be notified? ]
L134: 
L135: After you submit all required application documents, your admission review typically takes about 3–10 business days, depending on your academic level and program.
L136: 
L137: You’ll receive your official admission decision by email from the Office of Admission, and then your enrollment coach will reach out to walk you through your next steps and answer any questions.
L138: #### [Button: What if I need to start in a later term? ]
L139: 
L140: If you are admitted but decide to start in a later trimester, you may defer your start for up to one year from your original admission term. To change your start term, simply email apply@umassglobal.edu and request the “After-Admit Change of Start Term Request” form when you are ready to enroll.​
L141: Please note: if you are admitted to the Doctor of Education (Ed.D.) in Organizational Leadership program and do not start in the term to which you were admitted, you will need to submit a new application for a future term.
L142: #### [Button: Where can I submit my application documents? ]
L143: 
L144: After submitting your online application, additional required documents can be sent the following ways:
L145: 
L146: Email: apply@umassglobal.edu
L147: 
L148: Mail: University of Massachusetts Global
L149: ATTN: Office of Admission
L150: 65 Enterprise, Suite 150
L151: Aliso Viejo, CA 92656
L152: 
L153: 
L154: Please do not email test scores or transcripts unless sent directly from the registrar’s office of your former learning institution.
L155: 
L156: ### Credit for Prior Learning
L157: #### [Button: What is Credit for Prior Learning? ]
L158: 
L159: Credit for Prior Learning may help you earn credit for learning completed outside a traditional college course. Depending on your program and the learning you can document, this may include military training, professional certifications, workforce training, qualifying exams, ACE-recommended learning, or portfolio assessment.
L160: 
L161: UMass Global reviews your documentation and determines whether credit may apply to your degree.
L162: #### [Button: Does an ACE recommendation mean I will receive credit? ]
L163: 
L164: Not always. An ACE recommendation can show that your learning may be eligible for review. UMass Global decides whether credit applies to your degree based on your documentation, program requirements, and current academic policies.
L165: #### [Button: How much Credit for Prior Learning can I apply to my undergraduate degree? ]
L166: 
L167: Credit from other credit opportunities is generally limited to 25% of the credits required for an undergraduate degree. That is up to 15 credits in a 60-credit associate degree or up to 30 credits in a 120-credit bachelor’s degree.
L168: Some types of credit are not included in this limit, including ACE-evaluated credit and eligible AP, CLEP, DSST, IB, DLAT, and DLPT exams. Program requirements and residency requirements may still apply.
L169: ### Transcripts
L170: 
L171: #### [Button: Can I use my unofficial transcripts to be admitted? ]
L172: 
L173: Yes, we can start processing your application with your unofficial transcripts. You may upload them to the Education History section of the online application for admission or email them to admtranscripts@umassglobal.edu to expedite your admission.
L174: 
L175: Official transcripts are still required and must be submitted by the end of your first session.
L176: #### [Button: What is an "official" transcript? ]
L177: 
L178: An official transcript is one sent directly from the institution of record to University of Massachusetts Global.
L179: 
L180: #### Electronic Transcripts
L181: 
L182: Electronic transcripts must be sent from your previous institution directly to us - University of Massachusetts Global Admissions Office at admtranscripts@umassglobal.edu. Electronic transcripts that have been emailed to the applicant and then forwarded to the Admissions Office are not considered official.
L183: #### Paper Transcripts
L184: 
L185: Paper transcripts sent via mail must arrive at UMass Global's Admissions Office in a sealed envelope from the institution of record. A transcript issued to the applicant may be accepted if it is delivered in the official unopened and sealed envelope from the institution of record.
L186: 
L187: #### [Button: Do all programs require transcripts? ]
L188: 
L189: No. Transcripts are not required for the added authorization credential programs, or the California Teacher of English Learners (CTEL) authorization.
L190: #### [Button: What transcripts are required to be submitted for admission? ]
L191: 
L192: Admission requirements vary by program. Check the 【15†current catalog†catalog.umassglobal.edu】 for specific requirements related to your program of interest. When filling out the online application, you must list your complete academic history regardless of the transcript requirements. This includes all colleges, universities, career institutions, military institutions, etc., where you earned academic credit.
L193:   * Undergraduate: If you are applying to any of our undergraduate programs, transcripts are required from all institutions previously attended.
L194:   * Graduate: If you are applying to one of our graduate programs, we require you to submit transcripts from the highest level, most recently earned degree from an institutionally accredited institution (bachelor's, master's, or doctoral). If graduate-level or credential coursework was taken after the bachelor’s degree, regardless of whether a master’s or other graduate-level degree or credential was completed, those transcripts are required in addition to the bachelor’s degree transcripts.
L195: #### [Button: Do I order my own transcripts? ]
L196: For undergraduate applicants: UMass Global will attempt to order official transcripts from all institutions you list on your application whenever those schools allow authorized third-party ordering. Please review the 【54†Transcript Guidelines】 for details on which transcripts are required and how they must be sent. Some institutions do not permit third-party requests, so be sure to monitor your email for confirmations and any notices that you may need to order a transcript yourself.
L197: For graduate applicants: If you are applying to a School of Education program, UMass Global will also attempt to order official transcripts from all institutions listed on your application, subject to each school’s third-party ordering policies. For all other graduate programs, you are responsible for ordering and sending your official transcripts directly, following the same 【54†Transcript Guidelines】 and any instructions sent to you by email.
L198: ### Transferring Existing Credits
L199: #### [Button: What is the Academic Fresh Start Option? ]
L200: 
L201: This admission option is allowed for newly or readmitted undergraduate students who believe that their historical academic performance is not reflective of their current demonstrated ability to be successful. The option will ignore all academic coursework at any institution of higher education 10 or more years prior to the time of applying. It can only be used at the point of admission or readmission to University of Massachusetts Global.
L202: Once admitted under academic fresh start, the student will not receive credit for courses taken ten or more years prior to the date of admission to University of Massachusetts Global. Ignored coursework cannot be used to satisfy prerequisite or degree requirements at University of Massachusetts Global.
L203: #### [Button: How will my previous college credits be transferred into my degree? ]
L204: 
L205: UMass Global accepts general education block transfers from institutionally accredited colleges or universities in accordance with state standards and participates in the California Community College “Degree with a Guarantee” program. Use our comprehensive 【55†coursework transfer database†services.umassglobal.edu】 to look up courses you've taken and determine how they may apply to UMass Global required courses.
L206: For those who are applying to a 【56†UMass Global MyPath】 the process of evaluating existing credit includes:
L207:   * Prior coursework with a minimum grade of B- or better from institutionally accredited institutions will first be evaluated against UMass Global’s credit-hour-based courses.
L208:   * Once prior credit has been determined to be equivalent to UMass Global’s credit hour-based program, the university will then determine whether you will receive transfer credit for any of the competencies in the MyPath program.
L209:   * Prior transfer credits must be applicable to the MyPath program and count toward its graduation requirements.
L210: #### [Button: UMass Global MyPath: Will I get credit in the program for my work or “life” experience? ]
L211: 
L212: UMass Global MyPath programs are specifically designed to allow you to leverage existing skills and knowledge as you progress through your degree. Here's how it works:
L213:   * Many competencies start with an assessment to set a knowledge baseline. The program then adapts itself according to your specific skills. You can spend more time concentrating on the areas where you need more growth and less time on topics you know well, allowing you to complete the program at a potentially quicker pace.
L214:   * Although prior life experience cannot directly satisfy academic credit and official degree requirements, the skills that you have learned in the real world can definitely help you potentially pace through the program faster.
